title: Hybrid queue-drain microbatching and kernel probe to cut embeddings tail latency
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Short problem statement: p99 embedding latency spikes under mixed small/large requests during peak traffic. Root causes suspected: inefficient queue draining that leaves small requests waiting for large microbatches, suboptimal kernel selection for short sequences, and head-of-line blocking when KV cache misses occur. Proposed approach: implement hybrid queue-drain algorithm (priority-aware coalescing + time-bound drain windows), add lightweight kernel-probing at the start of a batch to select fast-path kernels for short sequences, and introduce an early-completion hint path for single-item low-length requests.
acceptance_criteria: P99 reduced by >=30% vs baseline for production embedding endpoint under synthetic mixed workload
P95 and P50 maintain or improve, with throughput within 10% of baseline
No regression in quality of embeddings or reranking scores (automated evals green)
End-to-end canary rollout with automated fallback and telemetry
work_log: 2026-02-12: Ticket created by Ava Martinez after investigating Friday incident (embedding p99 spike).
2026-02-13: Profiling pass with Daniel Kim — identified queue depth correlation with tail events; preliminary microbench of small-seq kernel shows 1.8x speedup when using fast-path.
2026-02-16: Spike weekend runbook: throttled large requests; began spike-safe canary plan.

2026-02-18: Design review with Priya, Liam, Sofia — agreed on hybrid drain with 4ms bounded wait and priority coalescing heuristic. Decided to pursue kernel probe instead of full model variant routing to reduce complexity.
2026-02-20: Prototype implemented: emb-queue-drain v0 with time-bound window and sequence-length histograming. Unit tests added.
2026-02-24: Benchmarks run in staging cluster (see benchmark_results). Observed p99 improvements but regressions for very large batch throughput; tuned drain window to 8ms for better amortization.
analysis: Profiling notes: tail events are dominated by batches that mix 1-3 token short requests with 512-token requests. The scheduler currently waits for batch targets causing small requests to wait >50ms.

Kernel probe idea: for each candidate batch, run a fast microkernel selector sampling first token shapes and choose specialized kernel when >70% short sequences detected. Probe cost measured ~0.4ms per batch.
KV cache misses add ~6-12ms variance. Adding small parallel prefetch for likely keys reduces variance but increases memory pressure.
Trade-offs: tighter drain windows reduce p99 but increase throughput overhead and small increase in token cost due to less full batching.
benchmark_results: Baseline (prod-like mixed workload): p50=7.6ms p95=18.2ms p99=128.7ms throughput=120K req/min
v0 prototype (4ms drain, kernel probe disabled): p50=8.0ms p95=16.9ms p99=89.3ms throughput=112K req/min
v1 tuned (8ms drain, kernel probe enabled): p50=8.2ms p95=15.6ms p99=78.1ms throughput=106K req/min
Quality regression check: rerank AUC delta <0.002 across 3 eval sets
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Merge feature flags behind 'emb.hybrid_drain' and 'emb.kernel_probe' - internal canary in dedicated clusters
Stage 2: 2% traffic canary in us-west with telemetry and automatic rollback on p99 regression
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 25% over 48 hours with continuous health checks (latency, errors, customer signals)
Stage 4: Full rollout with alerting thresholds tightened for 24h, then relax
risks: Throughput regressions for large-batch-heavy workloads if drain window is too short
Memory pressure from aggressive KV prefetch leading to evictions on dense hosts
Edge-case where kernel probe chooses slow kernel due to noisy sample distribution
Operational complexity: new knobs may confuse on-call during incidents
next_steps: Finalize probe heuristics (sample size, thresholds) and add A/B benchmark for different probe costs
Add telemetry hooks to measure probe decision accuracy and downstream kernel latency
Tune drain window per-instance based on observed sequence-length distribution (adaptive window)
Prepare canary dashboard and SLO-based rollback automation
Coordinate with platform team to validate Dedicated capacity behavior under tuned config
